Now let me take you through the operational and financial performance of Jindal Saw and its 
key major subsidiaries for the second quarter of FY27, with a focus on the key developments 
that are shaping our business performance and future growth prospects.  
 
In today's presentation, we will cover three key areas. First, the financial performance, which 
the board has approved on last Friday. This is for Q2 of FY27 and H1 of FY27. Second, the 
business scenario and outlook. And third, update on the new projects in MENA region. Through 
this discussion, we aim to provide you with the key perspective on our performance, business 
priorities, and growth opportunities going forward.  
 
Now let me first present the high-level summary for the Q2 FY27, comparing it with the Q1 
FY27 and the corresponding quarter in the previous year. During Q2 FY27, the company 
delivered improved top line, with gross revenue hitting INR3,881 crores, which is up by 3% on 
quarter-to-quarter basis, and 14% year-on-year basis. However, operational has been 
compressed, the EBITDA to INR265 crores, down from INR341 crores in Q1 of FY27, and 
INR335 crores, which was in Q2 of FY 2026.

and INR80 crores in Q2 of FY26. This is net of a INR27 crores tax credit received during the 
quarter.  
 
Financial performance on a standalone basis for H1 '27 and H1 of FY26: the company delivered 
improved top-line momentum in the first half of H1 FY27, with gross revenues rising 13% year-
on-year to INR7,637 crores, up from INR6,736 crores in H1 of the previous year, which is FY26. 
However, operating profitability faced pressure, as EBITDA contracted to INR606 crores from 
INR894 crores in the similar period last year.  
 
On a positive note, finance costs fell to INR163 crores from INR239 crores in H1 of FY26, 
showcasing efficient capital management despite INR depreciation against the USD. Ultimately, 
higher tax expense in lower operating margins impacted the bottom-line performance of the 
company. PBT finished at INR189 crores, down from INR412 crores, while the PAT landed at 
INR181 crores, compared to INR443 crores in H1 '26. 
A reflection of INR8 crores tax expenses this half versus INR31 crores tax credit last year. 
Overall, H1 '27 has delivered a increase in the revenue and lower finance cost, although 
profitability remained under pressure due to lower operating earnings and couple of other things.  
 
On consolidated basis, this is we'll now discuss Q2 versus Q1 of FY27 with Q2 FY26. On a 
consolidated basis, gross open income increased by FY by just a sec. Okay, on a consolidated 
basis, our top-line expanded by its 0.8% sequentially to INR4,523 crores from INR4,476 crores 
in Q1 FY27 and rose 6% year-on-year basis from INR4,264 crores in Q2 FY26.  
The EBITDA slid to INR312 crores from INR420 crores in H1 in Q1 of FY27 and INR482 
crores fuel in FY26. Finance expenses rose 15.7% sequentially up INR17 crores to INR125 
crores from INR108 crores in Q1 FY27, although remained lower than INR153 crores which 
was logged in Q2 of FY26.  
PBT dropped to INR14 crores after the adjustment of the joint ventures and compared to INR143 
crores in the previous quarter and INR183 crores year-on-year. Profit after tax is reported at 
INR35 crores from INR91 crores in Q1 FY27 and INR139 crores in Q2 FY26. Notably, 
INR27crores tax credit caused PAT to surpass PBT by that amount. On consolidation basis, our 
top line continued it our top line continued on a higher side, with gross income expanding by 
8% to INR8999 crores. However, severe operating margin pressures impacted overall 
profitability.  
EBITDA declined by 37%, leading to a 5.9 percentage point contraction in EBITDA margin to 
8%, while a 27.8% reduction in finance costs, down to INR234 crores, offered some relief. 
Pretax savings, PBT after JV share, fell 72% to INR157 crores. Finally, the operational 
slowdown combined with higher tax provisions, resulted in a 77% EBITDA in profit after tax.

Now, what is the prognosis for these results? Overall, while our revenue increased, profitability 
got impacted. And the major reasons for this weaker performance are as under. Ongoing 
geopolitical tension in West Asia have worsened due to recent escalations in Saudi Arabia, a 
region where we hold significant export order exposure.  
The main challenge is not other order cancellation, but rather delay in shipping and revenue 
recognition. If these project delays delay persists, dedicated production facilities will remain 
underutilized and continue to drive up fixed and operational costs. Then second, the ongoing 
global conflict has driven up international and domestic logistics costs.  
This directly impacts our operations, particularly because most of the sales contracts are 
structured on a delivered basis, historically. Surging raw material costs, particularly for coking 
coal have squeezed margins in the DI pipe business. This pressure was further compounded by 
lower capacity utilization due to lower execution in water pipe business as softness in domestic 
water business continues. This resulted in the impact on the profitability.  
 
The Abu Dhabi DI plant is facing a combination of cost overrun, underutilization, and delivery 
constraints, including difficulties serving customers who cannot be reached through truck-based 
transportation. This resulted in lower production, sales and impact on profitability. In the 
seamless business. 
While the API license reinstated in June '26 for our eligibility for the key orders, though 
immediate financial impact remained limited in Q2. The seamless pipe business is currently 
bidding on new orders to rebuild its order book and is witnessing the improvement in the 
backlog.

infra water infra segment, increased raw material prices, increased logistics costs and other cost 
inflationary factors and also supply chain constraints rather than a single adverse factor.

Now let's talk a bit about our progress of our seamless pipe plant in Abu Dhabi. Jindal Saw 
proposed seamless pipe manufacturing project in KEZAD industrial area, Abu Dhabi, UAE is 
progressing to the initial development and construction phase. 
The project, with a proposed capacity of 300,000 tons per annum and an estimated investment 
of approximately USD330 million, is intended to strengthen the company's presence in Middle 
East oil and gas market. By securing a developed leasehold land with existing civil 
infrastructure, we have accelerated our construction timeline. 
Procurement of critical long-lead equipment is underway, supported by active Letter of Credit 
and initial cash advances. With financial closure projected in coming months, the project 
remains firmly on track to commence commercial operations in FY28-'29.  
Jindal Saw's Abu Dhabi strategy reflects a deliberate move to establish a strong regional 
manufacturing hub by combining seamless steel pipes for the oil and gas sector and ductile iron 
pipes for water sector infrastructure. 
This dual platform approach is strategically aimed at capitalizing on the Middle East long-term 
investments in energy security, hydrocarbon development, and water infrastructure, while 
strengthening customer proximity, enhancing regional market access, and creating a diversified 
platform for sustainable growth across the energy and water sectors.  
 
Regarding our SAW pipe plant in Saudi Arab, we communicated earlier also that we have 
established a strategic joint venture in Saudi Arabia, where Jindal Saw will hold 51% equity 
stake and Buhur of Kingdom of Saudi Arabia will hold 49%. 
The joint venture envisages setting up two advanced pipe manufacturing facilities, helical pipes 
and longitudinal pipes with a capacity of 300,000 metric ton each, catering to the region's 
growing water infrastructure and energy requirement. The project is progressing well. Land has 
been secured. LCs for long-lead items has been established. 
We remain focused on accelerating project execution, with interim financial closure expected 
on over the next few months. We recognize that prevailing geopolitical environment and 
heightened regional security concerns may create some near-term uncertainties around project 
execution, logistics, and investment timing. Nevertheless, our approach remains guided by the 
long-term fundamentals of Saudi Arabia's energy and water infrastructure requirements.

export routes that reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz. We remain committed to a
